hook_text: Two blocks, one rope zigzagging between them. The number of ropes under the load is your mechanical advantage.
clip_script: Top block on the beam. Bottom block on the bucket. One rope threads between them and comes down to your hand. Count the rope sections pulling up on the bottom block. Two: you pull half. Three: a third. Four: a quarter. The rope going to your hand from the top block does not count; it pulls on the beam. Pay in rope: advantage 4 means four metres hauled for one metre up. Measure it and you get a bit less than the count, because the bottom block weighs something and every wheel rubs. That gap is efficiency. Draw it, arrow every rope, count the up arrows.
visual_style: Whiteboard beam, two blocks, a rope zigzagging; load-bearing sections lit up one by one with a counter; the hand rope greyed out; a table of 2, 3, 4 with efforts 10, 7, 5.
mood: Clear and practical, like a workshop demonstration.
pacing: Rig, count, halve, third, quarter, the rope that does not count, pay in rope, the honest gap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build a tackle with two cotton reels and string.
